## The Difference Between Assistance and Dependence
URL: https://teawithree.com/tools-the-difference-between-assistance-and-dependence.html
Description: My favourite mornings begin with the tactile ritual of shutting my laptop, nudging a notebook towards me and making a single neat line down the margin. The gesture is small and domestic. It is also a test. Closing the laptop does not make the world less clever. What it does is remind me that some decisions need human attention, the sort of attention that cannot be outsourced to the pleasing certainty of a search result or an algorithmic nudge.

## What AI Can Give Back to a Human Day
URL: https://teawithree.com/tools-what-ai-can-give-back-to-a-human-day.html
Description: On the kitchen table this morning my laptop sat beside a sheaf of handwritten notes and a cooling cup of tea. The notes were flecked with scribbles and arrows and the kind of small, useful mistakes that tell you you have been thinking for yourself. The laptop offered a different kind of promise, pages of text waiting to be nudged into shape. I have been learning how to let the two coexist rather than compete. The question I keep returning to is not what AI can do for me but what it can give back to the human parts of my day.

## What a Nervous System Reset Really Means
URL: https://teawithree.com/wellbeing-nervous-system-reset.html
Description: Your nervous system is basically the body’s alarm and recovery system. It’s constantly scanning for threat or safety. When life piles on deadlines, notifications, arguments, traffic, old stress that never fully left it can get stuck in “on” mode. Heart rate up, muscles tight, mind racing, gut unsettled. That’s the sympathetic side running the show (fight, flight, or freeze).

## What My Oura Ring Taught Me About Sleep
URL: https://teawithree.com/wellbeing-what-my-oura-ring-taught-me-about-sleep.html
Description: There is a small circle of metal I take off the moment I wash my hands and rest on the bedside table beside whatever book I am reading. It is unobtrusive in a way a wristband is not. It feels private and a little companionable. Wearing it has not turned me into a perfect sleeper. What it has done is change how I notice sleep and how quickly I equate a number with either success or failure.

The way we frame a question sets the direction of everything that follows.
